Uther's Tomb. The Lightbringer is at rest here.

Centaur territory. Let's not pick a fight we don't need.

Valor's Rest. A graveyard for the ones who held this line.
We should be careful enough to not join them.
Valormok. Our camp under Azshara's cliffs.
Set your hearth in Valormok if we're staying.
Valorwind Lake. Pretty water, Hinterlands rules.
Don't let the quiet fool you.

Witch Hill. The farms out here have a bad name.

Watch out for the Frostmane trolls.

Good to see a friendly banner out here.
Elwynn Forest. Green, peaceful... mostly.
Mind the Defias. They're everywhere lately.

Faldir's Cove. A hidden beach under the cliffs.
Smugglers' water. Watch the landing.
The Fallow Sanctuary. Lost and overgrown.
I wouldn't wander off the path here.
Feathermoon Stronghold! Our island keep off the coast.

Feralas. Old night elf forest, older ruins.

Fire Plume Ridge. The crater's still cooking.

Firewatch Ridge. Dark Iron patrols like this overlook.
Good view of a bad place.
Frostsaber Rock. The cats den here.
Beautiful animals. Let's not startle them.
Gadgetzan! If you can pay, they can find it.

Gahrron's Withering. The eastern cauldron.
Nothing good grows here. Let's not test that.
Gnomeregan. The gnomes want their city back.
Radiation and leper gnomes. Stay close.
Golakka Hot Springs. Steaming water, short tempers.
Nice if you like your baths with elementals.
Goldshire! The Lion's Pride Inn is right there.
Set your hearth in Goldshire, it's central.
Gordunni Outpost. Ogres in Feralas.

The Grimesilt Dig Site. Still digging, somehow.
Dwarves. I have to respect the commitment.
Hearthglen. Scarlet Crusade ground.
They fight the Scourge. They also fight everyone else.
Hillsbrad. Southshore's just down the road.
The Forsaken at Tarren Mill are close. Careful.
Hive'Ashi. Close enough to the Hold to keep everyone awake.
Northern hive. Watch the swarms.
Hive'Regal. Do not go in lightly.
A great silithid hive. Stay out unless we mean it.
Hive'Zora. The western hive, no friendlier.
I hear them under the sand.
Ironforge! Warm forges and good ale.
The Great Forge. Bank and auction house are close.
Irontree Woods. The trees walk.
I would not chop anything in here.
The Isle of Dread. Naga and spray.
The name is doing a lot of work.
Jadefire Run. Satyrs, and they've been at this a long time.
Corruption with a smile. Let's not linger.
Jaedenar. Shadow Council, Legion, bad news.
The name alone is a warning. Stay together.
Jintha'Alor. A whole Vilebranch city on the cliffs.

Karazhan. Medivh's tower.
The lights are on. I would not knock.
Kharanos! The Thunderbrew Distillery is right there.
Set your hearth at the Thunderbrew, it's cosy.
The Kodo Graveyard. So many bones.

Lake Kel'Theril. Frozen Highborne ruins.
The ice has a memory. Walk carefully.
Lakeshire. Pretty lake, busy bridge.

The Lakkari Tar Pits. Things fall in.
Do not take a shortcut across the tar.
Lethlor Ravine. Black dragons like this canyon.
I would not camp here. Just saying.
Light's Hope Chapel. A small light in a dark land.
The Argent Dawn holds this ground. I'm glad someone's here.
Loch Modan. The big dam is something, huh?
Troggs everywhere. Thelsamar has the quests.
Lost Rigger Cove. Southsea pirates.
They'll rob us if we let them. Let's not let them.
Mannoroc Coven. Demons, and lots of them.
This place feels wrong. Let's not linger.
Maraudon. The centaur's cavern temple. Stay together.
Theradras is down there somewhere. Watch your step.

Mazthoril. Blue dragons live in there.
Knock softly. Or maybe don't knock at all.
Menethil Harbor. Boats to Auberdine and Theramore.
Set your hearth in Menethil, it's the crossroads.
The Molten Core. Ragnaros is down there.
I would not go in without a small army.
Moonglade. The druids hid this valley well.
Quiet, moonlit, and a relief after Felwood.
Morgan's Vigil. Our camp on the eastern edge.
Set your hearth at Morgan's Vigil if we're staying in the ash.
Nesingwary's camp. He hunts anything that moves.

Set your hearth in Nethergarde. These walls are a comfort.

A good place to rest, if we can be still.
Nijel's Point. Our holdfast in these hills.
Set your hearth at Nijel's Point for Desolace.
Noonshade Ruins. Wastewander ground.
Bandits in the ruins. At least the shade is honest.

Wave to the Dawn, then keep going.

Kobolds in the mine and wolves in the woods. Classic.

If anything under these trees stays quiet.
The Pillar of Ash. Easy to see, hard to like.
A burned landmark in a burned land.
Plaguewood. Sick trees, worse shadows.
Stratholme is close. Stay together.
The Pool of Tears. The temple sits out there.
Wide water, worse shores. Watch the banks.

Redridge. Gnolls and orcs in the hills.
Lakeshire needs a lot of help.

Demon ground. I already want to leave.

I wouldn't camp in these streets.

The naga never really left this shore.

Grab the flight path to Darnassus' docks.

Good lookout. Bad picnic spot.

Set your hearth in Southshore for Hillsbrad.

The night elves here watch the ruins and the dragons.
Steamwheedle Port. Fish, docks, and deals.
A goblin harbor. Keep one hand on your coin purse.
Stormwind! Bank, trainers, auction house.
The heart of the Alliance. Mind the canals.

Scourge in one half, Scarlets in the other. Watch every door.
Stromgarde Keep. A broken kingdom, still worth the trip.
Syndicate, ogres, and leftovers. Careful in the ruins.
The Swamp of Sorrows. Green, wet, and full of bad ideas.

Tabetha's Farm. A mage in the middle of the swamp.
I would not pick a fight with the woman who lives here.
Talonbranch Glade. Our camp in northern Felwood.
Close to Timbermaw Hold. Be polite on the way through.

Big temple, bigger residents.
The Sunken Temple. Hakkar's name is still on it.
Green dragons sank this for a reason. Stay close.
Terror Run. The big dinosaurs run here.
If the ground shakes, that's not weather.

A broken village in the Plaguewood. Let's not add to it.
Thalanaar. A lonely post looking out on Thousand Needles.

The Altar of Zul. High, old, and unfriendly.

The Crystal Vale. Pretty, and strange.

The Fungal Vale. Mushrooms, and worse.
I would not touch anything in this hollow.

Careful, the last boss fears. Clear the room first.

They've had a long road to end up here.

Good place to see trouble coming.

Watch the cliffs. And everything in the trees.

The Sunken Temple. Hakkar's name is still on it.
Green dragons sank this for a reason. Stay close.

Thelsamar. Grab the flight path.

Thistleshrub Valley. Thorns, elementals, no shade.
I already don't like it.

Grab the flight path. And maybe a drink of water.

Timbermaw Hold. Earn the furbolg's trust, or stay out.
The tunnel to Winterspring. Be polite in there.
The Twilight Base Camp. They preach the end of everything.

They won't be glad to see us. Or anyone.

Valor's Rest. A graveyard for the ones who held this line.

Winterspring. Snow, silence, and the occasional dragon.

Agamand Mills. The Agamand family fell to the plague, and now they walk their own fields as undead.

The Altar of Storms in the Burning Steppes, a warlock's rise where the ground itself feels listened-to.

Auberdine, the night elves' harbor town on Darkshore.

Booty Bay, a goblin pirate port carved into a cliff. Watch your purse.
Brackenwall Village, the ogre-built Horde town in western Dustwallow Marsh.
Brambleblade Ravine. Quilboar have dug in here among the thorns.

Camp Taurajo, a tauren camp on the southern Barrens.
The Caverns of Time, a bronze dragon shrine hidden in the Tanaris mountains, where the past is not as still as it looks.

Corin's Crossing, a ruined crossroads in the Eastern Plaguelands, thick with the Scourge.
Crown Guard Tower, an Argent Dawn tower watching the road through the Eastern Plaguelands.
Dalson's Tears, a ruined farm and another Scourge cauldron in the Western Plaguelands.
Darkshire. The Night Watch guards this town from the horrors of the woods.
Darkshore. A long, misty coast of ancient night elf ruins, and the furbolgs here have been corrupted.
Darkwhisper Gorge, a deep, fel-touched cut in southern Winterspring. Something down there is listening.

Deathknell. Forsaken who break free of the Lich King's control wake here, in the old graveyard.
Desolace. A blasted, ashen land the night elves once called a garden. The centaur clans still war over what's left.

Dolanaar, a quiet night elf village on Teldrassil.
Dreadmaul Hold, an ogre fortress in the Blasted Lands, close enough to the Portal to be a bad idea.
Dreadmaul Rock, an ogre mound in the Burning Steppes, under a constant rain of ash.
Drygulch Ravine. The harpies have made it their roost, so watch the cliffs.
Dun Modr, a dwarven hold in the north of the Wetlands, overrun by the Dark Iron dwarves.
Dun Morogh. Snowy mountain valleys in the land of the dwarves and gnomes.
Durnholde Keep. Thrall was raised there as a slave and a gladiator, before he broke free.
Durotar. Thrall named this land for his father, Durotan, when he led the freed orcs to Kalimdor. It's harsh and red, but it's theirs.
Duskwood. This forest was once part of Elwynn, but darkness fell over it, and now the dead and the worgen roam.
Dustwallow Marsh. A foggy stretch of mud and crocolisks on Kalimdor's east coast, with Theramore on one shore and ogres in the west.
The Eastern Plaguelands. The worst of the Scourge's work on Lordaeron: plague cauldrons, ruined towns, and Stratholme at the end of the road.
Eastvale Logging Camp, on Elwynn's eastern edge near Redridge.
Eastwall Tower, another Argent Dawn lookout in the Eastern Plaguelands.
The Echo Isles were the Darkspear trolls' home, until the witch doctor Zalazane turned to dark voodoo and enslaved his own people.
Elwynn Forest, the green heart of the kingdom of Stormwind. It was burned in the First War and has been rebuilt since.
The Emerald Sanctuary, an Emerald Circle camp in southern Felwood, trying to heal a forest that does not want to heal.
Ethel Rethor, a lonely stretch of Desolace shoreline, with old elven ruins in the water.
Everlook, a goblin town in the snows of Winterspring. Warm rooms, high prices, and a very welcome fire.
Faldir's Cove, a hidden beach under the Arathi cliffs, used by sailors who don't want to be found.
The Fallow Sanctuary, a lost, overgrown corner of the Swamp of Sorrows.
Fargodeep Mine. Kobolds have taken over the tunnels. You no take candle!
Feathermoon Stronghold, a night elf keep on an island off the Feralas coast.
Felstone Field, a plagued farm in the west, still watched by the Scourge cauldron.
Felwood. This was once a living night elf forest. The Legion's corruption turned it sick and green, and it hasn't recovered.
Feralas. Ancient night elf rainforest on Kalimdor's west coast, older than the Sundering, with the ruined city of Eldre'Thalas at its heart.
Fire Plume Ridge, the volcanic heart of Un'Goro, still breathing smoke and fire elementals.
Firewatch Ridge, a burned overlook in the Searing Gorge, watched by Dark Iron patrols.
Flame Crest, a Horde camp on a burned rise in the Burning Steppes.
Freewind Post. The tauren built it on top of the needles, linked by rope bridges.
Frostsaber Rock, where the frostsabers den in Winterspring, and the night elf huntresses know them by name.
Gadgetzan, a goblin town in the Tanaris sand. If you can pay, they can find it.
Gahrron's Withering, the eastern cauldron farm in the Western Plaguelands. Nothing good grows here.
Ghost Walker Post, a tauren camp watching the roads and the centaur in central Desolace.
Gnomeregan was the gnomes' great city, until troggs rose up from below. Mekkatorque flooded it with radiation to stop them, and it's been lost ever since.
Go'Shek Farm, a Horde farm in the Highlands, right on the edge of trouble.
Gol'Bolar Quarry, a dwarven quarry overrun by troggs.
Golakka Hot Springs, steaming pools in western Un'Goro, watched by elementals and the odd brave researcher.
Goldshire, the busy crossroads town of Elwynn. Everyone ends up at the Lion's Pride Inn eventually.
The Gordunni Outpost. Ogres have claimed this part of Feralas, and they do not share.
The Grimesilt Dig Site, where dwarves keep digging in the Gorge no matter how hot it gets.
Grom'gol Base Camp, the Horde's base in Stranglethorn.
Hammerfall, a Horde town built from an internment camp in the Arathi Highlands.
Hearthglen, a Scarlet Crusade hold in the Western Plaguelands. They fight the Scourge, and nearly everyone else.
Hillsbrad Foothills. Rolling farmland split between Southshore and Tarren Mill, and both sides want it.
Hive'Ashi, the northern silithid hive in Silithus, close enough to Cenarion Hold to keep everyone awake.
Hive'Regal, a great silithid hive in eastern Silithus. Do not go in lightly.
Hive'Zora, the western silithid hive in Silithus, no friendlier than the others.
Ironforge, carved into the heart of the mountain. King Magni Bronzebeard rules from the great forge.
Irontree Woods. The trees here walk, and they are not gentle about it.
The Isle of Dread, south of Feralas, where naga and old ruins wait in the spray.
Jadefire Run, a satyr camp in Felwood. They have been corrupting this forest for a long time.
Jaedenar. The Shadow Council and the Legion took this ruined barrow, and the name itself is a curse.
Jangolode Mine, held by the Defias.
Jasperlode Mine, another mine lost to kobolds.
Jintha'Alor, a great Vilebranch troll city terraced into the Hinterlands cliffs.
Karazhan, Medivh's tower in Deadwind Pass. The lights are still on. That is not comforting.
Kargath, the Horde's outpost in the Badlands, named for a great orc warrior.
Kharanos, a cozy dwarf town. The Thunderbrew brewery keeps it warm.
The Kodo Graveyard, where the great beasts come to die. The earth is white with their bones.
Lake Kel'Theril, a frozen Highborne ruin in Winterspring. The ice has a memory.
Lakeshire, a lakeside town that keeps getting raided by orcs and gnolls.
The Lakkari Tar Pits in northern Un'Goro. Things fall in. They do not always climb out.
Lethlor Ravine, a blackened canyon in the eastern Badlands, watched by the black dragonflight.
Light's Hope Chapel, the Argent Dawn's hold in the Eastern Plaguelands. It's a small light in a very dark land.
Loch Modan. The great Stonewrought Dam holds back the loch, and the dwarves guard it closely.
Lost Rigger Cove, a Southsea pirate hideout on the Tanaris shore.
Lushwater Oasis. The oases of the Barrens appeared along with the druids' work in the caverns below, and something is wrong with them now.
Maestra's Post, a sentinel outpost in northern Ashenvale.
Mannoroc Coven. Demons crawl over these ruins, and the ground itself feels wrong.
Maraudon. A vast cavern temple of the earth, claimed by the Maraudine centaur and fouled by the princess Theradras.
Marshal's Refuge, a cave camp in Un'Goro Crater, full of goblins, gnomes, and very stubborn researchers.
Mazthoril, a blue dragon cave in Winterspring. They are not always in the mood for visitors.
Menethil Harbor, a human port where ships sail for Kalimdor and Theramore.
The Molten Core, Ragnaros's prison and palace under Blackrock, where the Firelord was summoned and never sent back.
Moonbrook. The Defias own this town now, and the Deadmines lie beneath it.
Moonglade. A hidden, moonlit valley the druids kept safe through every war. Nighthaven sits quiet under the trees.
Morgan's Vigil, an Alliance camp on the eastern edge of the Burning Steppes.
Mulgore, the tauren homeland. Cairne Bloodhoof led the tribes here after the orcs helped them drive back the centaur.
Nesingwary's Expedition. Hemet Nesingwary hunts the biggest game in the jungle.
Nethergarde Keep, a Kirin Tor and Alliance fortress watching the Dark Portal in the Blasted Lands.
Nighthaven, the druids' village in Moonglade. Even the inn feels like it's listening to the moon.
Nijel's Point, an Alliance holdfast in the hills of northern Desolace.
Noonshade Ruins, Wastewander bandit ground in the Tanaris waste.
Northpass Tower, the northern Argent Dawn tower on the Plaguelands road.
Northshire Abbey, where the Light's priests and paladins train Stormwind's newest heroes.
Northshire Valley. The abbey's priests train new recruits here before sending them out into Elwynn.
Northwatch Hold, a Theramore fort on the Barrens' eastern coast.
Orgrimmar, the capital of the Horde. Thrall built it and named it for Orgrim Doomhammer, the Warchief who came before him.
Owl Wing Thicket, a quiet, wooded hollow in Winterspring, if anything under these trees stays quiet.
Palemane Rock. The Palemane gnolls hole up here and raid the plains.
The Pillar of Ash, a burned landmark in the Burning Steppes, easy to see and hard to like.
Plaguewood, a thick, sick forest in the north of the Eastern Plaguelands, in the shadow of Stratholme.
The Pool of Tears, the wide water around the Sunken Temple. Watch the shore.
Pyrewood Village. The villagers are cursed, and when night falls they turn into worgen.
Ragefire Chasm runs right under Orgrimmar. Troglodytes and Burning Blade cultists lurk in its burning caves.
Ratchet, a goblin port of the Steamwheedle Cartel. Gold matters more than banners here.
Raven Hill. The cemetery here doesn't keep its dead in the ground.
Raven Hill Cemetery. The dead don't rest here.
Razor Hill. A fortified orc town that keeps watch over Durotar's coast.
Razorfen Downs. The Scourge has crept into the quilboar's home, and their dead don't stay buried.
Razorfen Kraul. The quilboar live inside giant thorny vines. They say they grew from the body of the demigod Agamaggan.
Rebel Camp, on the jungle's northern edge.
Red Cloud Mesa, where the tauren raise their young under the open sky.
The Redridge Mountains. Blackrock orcs and gnolls raid down from the hills.
Refuge Pointe, the League of Arathor's camp in the Highlands.
Revantusk Village, a troll port on the Hinterlands coast, loyal to the Horde.
The Rise of the Defiler, a demon's rise in the Blasted Lands. You can feel it before you see it.
The Ruins of Alterac. The old capital sits broken in the mountains, and Crushridge ogres live in the halls.
The Ruins of Andorhal. The Scourge hasn't finished with this town, and it shows.
The Ruins of Eldarath, a drowned Highborne city on Azshara's coast.
The Ruins of Isildien, crumbling night elf stone deep in Feralas.
Rut'theran Village, at the foot of Teldrassil, where boats leave for Darkshore.
Saldean's Farm, one of the last families still farming in Westfall.
Sandsorrow Watch, a lonely rise over the western dunes of Tanaris.
The Scarlet Monastery. The Scarlet Crusade hates all undead and trusts no one, living or not.
Scholomance, a school of necromancy beneath Caer Darrow, run by the Cult of the Damned.
Searing Gorge. A burned, slag-choked canyon the Dark Iron dwarves carved under Blackrock, still coughing smoke into the sky.
Sen'jin Village is named for the old Darkspear witch doctor Sen'jin. He gave his life when Thrall helped his people escape to Kalimdor.
Sentinel Hill. The People's Militia holds out here against the Defias.
Seradane, an ancient part of the Hinterlands forest the green dragons still watch.
Shadowfang Keep. The archmage Arugal summoned the worgen here, and Baron Silverlaine's keep fell under his madness.
Shadowglen, where young night elves begin their training among the branches.
Shadowprey Village, a troll port on Desolace's coast. It's one of the few green places left in this land.
Shadra'Alor, a troll temple in the Hinterlands dedicated to the spider loa Shadra.
Shatter Scar Vale, where infernals fell during the Third War and the ground never cooled.
The Shrine of Remulos, a druid shrine in Moonglade watched by the son of Cenarius.
Silithus. A wind-scoured waste at the foot of Ahn'Qiraj, where the silithid hive and the Twilight's Hammer both want you gone.
Silverpine Forest. Gray woods between Lordaeron and the great wall of Gilneas. Worgen prowl here now.
Skull Rock. The Burning Blade cultists hide in these caves, still serving the demons the orcs fought to escape.
Sorrow Hill, a graveyard in the Western Plaguelands, close to Uther's Tomb.
Southshore, a human town on the coast of Hillsbrad that stands against the Forsaken.
Splintertree Post. Warsong orcs log Ashenvale from here, and the sentinels hate them for it.
Starfall Village, a night elf camp in Winterspring, watching the ruins and the dragons.
Steamwheedle Port, a goblin harbor on the Tanaris coast. Smells like fish and opportunity.
Stonard, the Horde's muddy outpost in the Swamp of Sorrows.
The Stonetalon Mountains. Peaks sacred to the druids, and the Venture Company is cutting them bare.
Stonetalon Peak, where the night elf druids keep their watch over the mountains.
Stonewatch Keep. The Blackrock orcs have taken it over.
The Stonewrought Dam. The dwarves built it to hold back the whole loch.
Stormwind City. The orcs destroyed it in the First War, and the stonemasons rebuilt it. Many of them were never paid, and that's how the Defias began.
Stranglethorn Vale. Jungle and ruins of the Gurubashi troll empire. It's beautiful, and it'll try to kill you.
Stratholme. Arthas purged this city, and the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade still fight over what's left of the streets.
Stromgarde Keep. Once the seat of a great human kingdom; now its walls are split between syndicates, ogres, and whoever is left.
Sun Rock Retreat, a Horde haven high in the Stonetalon peaks.
The Swamp of Sorrows. A green, sinking marsh on the edge of the Blasted Lands, and the trolls' Temple of Atal'Hakkar lies out in the water.
Tabetha's Farm, a mage's home in the middle of the marsh. She does not scare easily.
Talonbranch Glade, a night elf camp in northern Felwood, close to Timbermaw Hold.
Talrendis Point, a night elf post on Azshara's western edge.
Tanaris. An endless desert at the foot of Kalimdor, home to goblins, Wastewander bandits, and the lurking city of Zul'Farrak.
Tarren Mill. The Forsaken hold it now, just across the hills from Southshore.
Teldrassil. The night elf druids grew this great tree without the blessing of the dragons, and its roots don't feel quite right.
The Temple of Arkkoran, a sea-giant shrine on Azshara's shore.
The Temple of Atal'Hakkar, also called the Sunken Temple. Atal'ai trolls raised it to Hakkar, and the green dragons sank it for a reason.
Terror Run, where the biggest dinosaurs in Un'Goro make the earth shake.
Terrordale, a broken village in the Plaguewood. The name is not an exaggeration.
Thalanaar, a lonely night elf post on the eastern edge of Feralas, looking out over Thousand Needles.
The Altar of Zul, a high troll altar in the Hinterlands. The view is better than the company.
The Barrens. Dry grassland all the way across central Kalimdor, full of centaur, quilboar and harpies.
The Bulwark, the Argent Dawn and Forsaken line holding the edge of the Western Plaguelands.
The Cauldron, the slag pit at the heart of the Searing Gorge. Stay on the rims if you can.
The Crossroads. The Horde built this fort where the Barrens' main roads meet, and it's been fighting off raiders ever since.
The Crystal Vale, a strange, shining hollow in northern Silithus.
The Dark Portal. It was here the Horde first entered Azeroth, and the land around it has never been the same.
The Deadmines. Edwin VanCleef leads the Defias from a hidden harbor deep inside the mine.
The Forgotten Pools, another of the Barrens' strange oases.
The Fungal Vale, a sick, mushroom-choked hollow in the Eastern Plaguelands.
The Harborage, a quiet draenei camp hidden in the Swamp of Sorrows.
The Headland, a high ridge over the Alterac valley, with a long view and a cold wind.
The Hinterlands. Forested hills east of the Plaguelands, where the Wildhammer dwarves and the Vilebranch trolls have been neighbors for far too long.
The Marshlands, a wet, biting stretch of southern Un'Goro, thick with raptors and plants that bite back.
The Noxious Glade, a poisoned stretch of the Eastern Plaguelands near the plaguewoods.
The Quagmire. Deep mud, angry crocolisks, and very few dry paths.
The Sepulcher. The Forsaken hold this crypt as their outpost in Silverpine.
The Shimmering Flats. A huge salt flat where gnomes and goblins race their machines.
The Slithering Scar, a silithid hive-scar in southern Un'Goro. Watch the ground.
The Stockade, Stormwind's prison. The prisoners have rioted and taken it over.
The Temple of Atal'Hakkar, also called the Sunken Temple. Atal'ai trolls raised it to Hakkar, and the green dragons sank it for a reason.
The Twin Colossals, two huge rock pillars standing over western Feralas.
The Venture Company. Goblins who'll strip any land bare for profit, sacred ground or not.
Thelsamar, the dwarf town on Loch Modan's road.
Theramore Isle, Jaina Proudmoore's keep on the marsh. Ships from Menethil dock here.
Thistleshrub Valley, a dry, thorny basin in southern Tanaris, full of elementals and very little shade.
Thorium Point, a Thorium Brotherhood camp overlooking the Searing Gorge. They know the Dark Irons better than anyone.
Thousand Needles. A canyon of stone spires so tall they cast the whole valley in shadow.
Thunder Axe Fortress. The Burning Blade has a hold here, and they are not the welcoming kind.
Thunder Bluff. The tauren built their city on top of these mesas, and they ride lifts up and down the cliffs.
Thunder Ridge. Storms and thunder lizards, and very little shelter. Keep your head down.
Timbermaw Hold, the great furbolg tunnel through the mountains between Felwood, Winterspring, and Azshara. Earn their trust, or don't go in.
Tiragarde Keep. Kul Tiran soldiers built it after Admiral Proudmoore's fleet attacked Durotar, and some of them never left.
Tirisfal Glades was farmland of the kingdom of Lordaeron, until the Scourge swept through it. Now the Forsaken claim what's left.
The Twilight Base Camp, where the Twilight's Hammer preaches the end of everything in the Silithus waste.
Tyr's Hand, a great Scarlet Crusade city in the east. They trust almost no one who walks in alive.
Uldaman. A titan vault the dwarves cracked open, full of troggs, ancient stone, and secrets of the earthen.
Un'Goro Crater. A lost, steaming basin of dinosaurs and crystal pylons, sealed off from Tanaris by the mountains around it.
The Undercity lies beneath the ruins of Lordaeron's capital. Lady Sylvanas rules the Forsaken from its old crypts and sewers.
Uther's Tomb, where the Lightbringer was laid to rest after the fall of Lordaeron.
The Valley of Spears, a Maraudine stronghold in the canyons of Desolace.
The Valley of Trials. Young orcs and trolls prove themselves here before they're sent out into the world.
Valor's Rest, a graveyard in Silithus for those who came to hold the line against the hives.
Valormok, the Horde outpost in Azshara, under the cliffs of the old elven kingdom.
Valorwind Lake, a quiet stretch of water in the Hinterlands, when anything here can be called quiet.
The Wailing Caverns. Druids of the Fang went down there to heal the land, and the Emerald Dream's nightmare turned them.
The Western Plaguelands. Lordaeron's farmland, ruined by the Scourge. The fields still grow, but nothing that grows here is right.
Westfall was Stormwind's farmland. The farms were left empty and the Defias Brotherhood moved in.
The Wetlands. Swamps between Ironforge and Lordaeron, and the Dragonmaw orcs still hold Grim Batol.
Whelgar's Excavation Site, where dwarf explorers are digging up the past.
Winterfall Village, a hostile furbolg town in the Winterspring snow.
Winterspring. High, snowy country above Felwood, quiet under the trees until the Winterfall furbolg or the blue dragons remind you it isn't.
Witch Hill. The farmsteads out here have a bad name, and the wildlife is worse.
Zephras Isle, home of the Skyborne. I don't know much of its story yet, so let's learn it together.
Zoram'gar Outpost, a Horde foothold on Ashenvale's shore.
Zul'Farrak, the sand troll city in western Tanaris. The Farraki have been here longer than the goblins, and they have not forgiven anyone.
